The formula for the area of a sector of a circle is ½ r² θ where r is the radius of the circle and θ is the angle, in radians, contained by the sector. All sectors contained by the hexagon added together gives 720° or 4𝜋 in radians. 

∴ Area = ½ r² θ => ½ 1² 4𝜋 => ½ 4𝜋 = 2𝜋.

The radius(r) = 1 so each hexagon side length(𝓁 ) = 2. 

Adding all internal angles of the hexagon together = 720° or 4𝜋 in radians. 

The area of all circle sectors is ½r²4𝜋 = ½1²4𝜋 = 2𝜋. 

Hexagon area = ((3√3)÷2)×𝓁 ² = ((3√3)÷2)×2² = 6√3. 

∴ shared area = 6√3 - 2𝜋

I really like this slide of @kkirks from @LeanAgileScot 2015 based on some Buddhist characterisitcs of existence: 

The 3 characteristics of industry are:  
* everything is in a constant state of change 
* we need to collaborate 
* we will always battle dissatisfaction

"Lesson 5 is pilot on the plane ...he trains [to] deal with emergency situations. Like ambulance drivers and police ...they don't go to work thinking, 'I'm really gonna make myself happy today'. They go in to save lives, to make a difference ...or sometimes just to help" @kkirk

"[Next] ...we'd like to make certain people happy ...we wanna make key experts [and] managers happy. But this puts us in the position where we're making an upper class ...we're not really caring for people equanimously ...so then these people [use it] as a power mechanism" @kkirk

"[Next] ...we become obsessed with maintaining a feeling and in the process... we miss what's really happening. We miss seeing data. I'm eating so much chocolate cake, I want it so bad that I can't see the fact that I'm obese. So we end up suffering from wanting happiness" @kkirk
"So next, 1 of my favorite things - individuals are difficult to make and keep happy - anybody married? [audience laughs] ...making all these indiviuals happy is almost impossible" @kkirk

"I've got like 5 lessons... lesson 1 - happiness is prone to delusion" @kkirk 

[Slide reads "Danger: Outcome = happy" and shows the equation X+Y=Z where Z = we must be happy, X = infomation which is bad news, and that risks that you'll add Y = which is 'delusion' or 'ignorance']
When I 1st heard it, I thought it was a oneness with horses :-)

"...instead we might want to aim for equanimity. It's a state of mind, it's an attitude, rather than a fleeting emotion ...think about how many emotions we go thru in 1 day ...happiness is only just 1 emotion ...and we have a predisposition to look at the negative" @kkirk

"So in this talk what I'm trying to challenge here [is that] we're very obsessed with this whole idea of happiness. It's a good and honourable thing, don't get me wrong. But we are chasing a mood, yeah? And mood is not a reliable method of delivery. Just letting you know" @kkirk

An #unconference requires: 
•a theme 
•a diverse bunch of people 
•a compere (eg @LloydDavis) 
•1 big space and lots of breakout areas 
•Sharpies, Post-it notes and somewhere to stick them. 

Read more at https://www.ukgovcamp.com/2018/07/20/unconference-in-a-box/. 

#NuffSaid

An #unconference is also not difficult. It anything it’s easier than finding truly good speakers who really know how to give presentations (see http://www.doingpresentations.com/). Yes, pre-planning remains essential. You simply need much less pre-planning.

An #unconference is not a 1 hour, pre-arranged discussion in the middle 4 hour conference. It is not a bunch of parallel lightening talks with question and answer sessions. It is not a tick-box exercise. It is not an add-on. It is not a thing to be taken lightly.

#Unconference is slang for an all-day event that uses open space technology (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_Space_Technology). The concept’s been around for over 30 years and used by public sector for a large part of that. Permanent Secretaries and administrative assistants alike go to them.
What an #unconference is, and is not - a thread in 5 parts.

"The 2nd reason that multitasking can work is that learning 1 thing well can often help you do something else ..it's possible to cross train your mind.. If we want to become better ..spend some time doing something else, even if the 2 fields appear to be ..completely distinct"

"..how is it that some scientists are able to go on producing important work right thru their lives? ..the top scientists.. would shift topics repeatedly during their 1st 100 published research papers ..on average the most enduringly creative scientists switched topics 43 times"

"...what I'm describing here is having multiple projects on the go at the same time and you move backwards and forwards between topics as the mood takes you or as the situation demands... if we were willing to slow multitasking down we might find that it works quite brilliantly"

"I'd like to argue, that for an important kind of activity, doing 2 things at once, or 3 or even 4, is exactly what we should be aiming for.... it's very common among highly creative people... and I'd like to give it a name - slow motion multitasking" says @TimHarford
